h1: Before You Buy Another CRM, Find the Missing Quote
seo_title: What to Check Before Replacing Your CRM | NATA
meta_description: Diagnose where a customer record breaks, then test whether a workflow change, integration, or new CRM fixes it.
section_questions: How do you distinguish a software limit from a record problem?
What should a CRM vendor demonstrate with your workflow?
When does a replacement make commercial sense?
answer_capsule: Before replacing a CRM, reproduce the problem with real records and identify where it begins. Separate the definition of an account or opportunity, the behavior the team needs, missing integrations, and limits of the platform. Ask each option to pass the same test using cases your company actually handles.
takeaways: A real account that breaks in a way the business cares about.
A test from first entry through acceptance, delivery, or invoicing.
A view of the cost and responsibility after the software goes live.

faqs.question: Does low CRM adoption justify a switch?
faqs.answer: Find out why people leave it. It may be slower than their current method, omit a useful field, or require duplicate entry. Test a change on the actual work before deciding whether the platform is the limit.

faqs.question: Should every old record be migrated?
faqs.answer: Decide which history people need to keep using and which material belongs in a searchable archive. Test access and reconciliation for important records before switching.

faqs.question: What should you verify first after migration?
faqs.answer: Pick an active customer with an open quote and a recent order. Check the links, permissions, and next actions against the source records, then repeat with known edge cases.
